hypothesis: Detection is encoder/channel limited
evidence_available: Phase3A: E-small/E-base/E-large monotone on 6/6 metrics, detection most sensitive. Phase3C fixed-budget: encoder-heavy > balanced > Z-heavy (Budget-L mAP50 0.3204/0.3152/0.2639; Budget-M 0.3585/0.3462/0.3161) at LOWER FLOPs for encoder-heavy.
intervention: STEP3 per-object-size/per-distance recall for R0 vs R2 vs widths; cross-budget re-read of Phase3C by object size
prediction_if_true: The encoder advantage is concentrated on small and far objects, not uniform across sizes
falsification_criterion: If encoder gain is uniform across all size buckets, the advantage is generic capacity rather than a spatial/channel-specific bottleneck
decision: Do not retrain; decompose Phase3C checkpoints by object size

hypothesis: Detection is spatial-resolution limited
evidence_available: R0 det reads F2/F3/F4 at 1/8,1/16,1/32; R2 forces det through a single 1/8 Z and detection IMPROVES (+0.0339 mAP50 at z16). YOLOF: SiMo(35.0) vs MiMo(35.9), only -0.9 mAP.
intervention: STEP3 per-scale recall: R0 (multi-scale input) vs R2 (single 1/8 input), bucketed by GT box area
prediction_if_true: R2 loses recall on small objects relative to R0 while matching or beating R0 on large objects
falsification_criterion: If R0 and R2 have the same shape of recall-vs-size curve, resolution is not what separates them
decision: Test; if R2 small-object recall is not worse, resolution is secondary for detection

hypothesis: Detection is receptive-field/context limited
evidence_available: Probe B: dilation (2,4) reconstruction was WORSE than equal-parameter plain depth by 3.64x noise at 4ep; the plain-depth gain vanished at 20ep (-0.10x). Encoder already reaches 1/32.
intervention: STEP3 crowding/occlusion analysis: recall vs number of GT boxes per image, and vs max IoU overlap with another GT box
prediction_if_true: Recall degrades steeply with crowding/occlusion, and this degradation is not explained by object size alone
falsification_criterion: If recall is flat against crowding after controlling for size, context is not the binding constraint
decision: Cheap test; do not repeat dilation (explicitly forbidden as a repeat)

hypothesis: Detection is bottlenecked by the R2 reconstruction pathway (Z -> 3 scales), not by Z width
evidence_available: R0->R2 gap is +0.0339 mAP50 ALREADY at z16 (narrowest Z), so most of the change is not Z width. R2 also grows the det head 8406 -> 20918 params.
intervention: STEP4 parameter-matched reconstruction ladder at fixed z (rec complexity / det_ch), keeping total head params within 5%
prediction_if_true: Detection moves monotonically with reconstruction capacity at fixed z, and the R2-R0 gap is mostly attributable to reconstruction+head, not Z width
falsification_criterion: If detection is invariant to reconstruction complexity at fixed z and fixed head params, H4 is REJECTED
decision: Most informative single detection experiment; run only after STEP0-3 narrow the field

hypothesis: Lane is limited by the OUTPUT RESOLUTION at which its head operates (head runs on 1/8 features)
evidence_available: Model-free 1/8 ceiling (maxpool-by-8 then upsample) = 0.1853; trained models achieve lane fg IoU 0.1843/0.1882/0.1845 - statistically indistinguishable. GT erode1 survival 0.0107 (1-2 px wide). Pred/GT area = 3.37x. Recall 0.689 with precision ~0.20. Boundary tolerance 0/1/2 px -> IoU 0.184/0.382/0.460.
intervention: Lane-1/4-UP: bilinear upsample Z to 1/4, run the SAME lane head at 1/4 (no new information, identical parameters)
prediction_if_true: Lane fg IoU improves by >= 2x noise (0.0064) purely from operating resolution
falsification_criterion: If upsampling alone gives no gain, the ceiling is about INFORMATION at 1/4, not about head operating resolution
decision: This is the control that separates H5a from H5b - it must be run, not assumed

hypothesis: Lane is limited by the ABSENCE of 1/4 INFORMATION (Z is fused only from F2/F3/F4, all >= 1/8)
evidence_available: Encoder s1 emits a 1/4 feature map (160x160, 32 ch) but LightEncoder.forward does not return it; Z is built exclusively from 1/8 and deeper.
intervention: Lane-1/4-FEAT: add a 1x1 lateral from s1 (1/4) into the lane input, then run the lane head at 1/4 (+32*zc params, ~+0.5k at z16)
prediction_if_true: Lane fg IoU improves by >= 2x noise and BREAKS the 0.1853 ceiling that no channel change has moved
falsification_criterion: If real 1/4 features do not beat the 1/8 ceiling, lane is NOT spatially bounded and H5 must be REJECTED in favour of H6/H7/H8

hypothesis: There is a MINIMUM SUFFICIENT resolution: 1/4 is enough and 1/2 buys nothing extra
evidence_available: Section 8 of the Phase 5 brief: find the threshold, not the maximum.
intervention: Only run 1/2 if 1/4 shows a large gain
prediction_if_true: Lane-1/2 is within 1x noise of Lane-1/4
falsification_criterion: If 1/2 is clearly better, continue the ladder; if within noise, 1/4 is the threshold
decision: Do not run unless 1/4 shows a large effect; no full sweep

hypothesis: Lane is channel-capacity limited
evidence_available: z16/z32/z128 lane_fg = 0.1943/0.1992/0.2015 (z16->z128 = +0.0072 = 2.25x noise). Effective rank at z128 is 24.9% (31.93/128) - most channels redundant. Task projection 16->32 gave +0.0037 lane_fg at 20ep = 1.16x noise.
intervention: Control arm inside the lane resolution experiment: compare channel increase vs resolution increase at matched incremental FLOPs
prediction_if_true: Resolution gain per unit resource >> channel gain per unit resource
falsification_criterion: If a channel increase buys as much as the resolution increase, H6 is not subordinate to H5
decision: Reported as delta-metric / delta-resource, not as absolute score

hypothesis: Lane is supervision/loss limited
evidence_available: Lane positives are ~2089 px per 640x640 image = 0.51% of pixels. Model recall is already 0.689, i.e. it FINDS lanes and cannot place them.
intervention: Loss-side statistics only (no loss redesign): positive pixel ratio, share of lane loss coming from boundary pixels vs interior
prediction_if_true: A large majority of lane loss comes from a thin boundary band
falsification_criterion: If recall is high and precision is low, the defect is localisation, not supervision - H7 is REJECTED as dominant
decision: Statistics first; a loss intervention is only justified if the imbalance is extreme AND H5 fails

hypothesis: Lane is annotation/evaluation limited (the metric itself has a low ceiling)
evidence_available: Lane stroke 3.98 px train / 3.97 px val at 1280x720 (ratio 0.997) = 1.99 px at model input. Perfectly localised predictor of the correct width scores 0.973/0.972. Erosion survival k=1 0.069/0.065, k=2 0.0005. 71% of lane foreground is within 1 native px of the boundary and 99.9% within 2. Foreground spans 11 (train) / 14 (val) label values, four carrying 16-26% each, but EVERY class measures 3.3-4.1 px - geometrically homogeneous, semantically not.
intervention: Multi-tolerance ceiling ladder and a lane-width stratified analysis (thin vs wide lane instances)
prediction_if_true: The ceiling itself rises steeply with tolerance, confirming absolute lane IoU is metric-dominated
falsification_criterion: Not falsifiable in the usual sense - it is a measurement constraint that bounds every other lane claim
decision: REJECTED. The two splits agree to 0.3% and a correctly sized, perfectly located stroke scores 0.97, so the annotation is not the ceiling and the metric is not intrinsically unfair. The 1/8 grid is the ceiling. Retained only as a reporting rule: every lane number must be quoted with the 2 px-at-input stroke next to it, because readers will otherwise compare against datasets whose protocol widens lanes to 30 px before matching (CULane).

hypothesis: DA is channel-capacity limited
evidence_available: z16/z32/z128 da_fg = 0.7612/0.7736/0.7656, non-monotone. Phase3C: da_mIoU inside noise across all allocations (0.8490-0.8589). Probe C (lambda_det 0.2): +0.27x noise at z16, +0.01x at z32.
intervention: No new intervention - already saturated under channel, encoder, shared-Z and gradient interventions
prediction_if_true: REJECTED as the dominant DA bottleneck
falsification_criterion: Already falsified: four independent capacity interventions moved DA by less than 1x noise
decision: Do not spend GPU here; DA capacity work is closed

hypothesis: DA is spatial-resolution limited
evidence_available: 1/8 -> 1/4 block-fill reference for DA is 0.8753 -> 0.9410, so resolution offers 0.07-0.13. But r0_z16 scores 0.7699 against a 1/8 block-fill reference of 0.8801: it is 0.11 BELOW the score of the trivial 'paint every touched cell' strategy. Boundary band at the model's real granularity (16 native px = one 1/8 cell) holds 28.4% of DA foreground; at 8 px only 14.7%.
intervention: Per-band 1/8 ceiling vs per-band achieved IoU (STEP2)
prediction_if_true: If DA at 1/4 approaches 0.87, resolution is the dominant DA bottleneck
falsification_criterion: Achieved IoU stays ~0.11 below its own per-band ceiling at every band -> resolution is not what keeps DA down
decision: REJECTED. The model has not reached the resolution-defined bar, so raising the bar cannot be the fix. Do not spend a training run on DA resolution.

hypothesis: DA is far-field semantic/context limited
evidence_available: After cropping to the letterbox content rows 140-500 and using equal-mass bands, far / mid / near DA agree within noise and R0 is not better than R2 in the far band. The earlier far-field collapse was measured on grey padding.
intervention: STEP2: per-band 1/8 ceiling, per-band mixed-block fraction (blocks containing both fg and bg at 1/8), per-band GT area, per-band boundary-to-area ratio
prediction_if_true: Far field sits much further BELOW its own local ceiling than mid/near do, and the mixed-block fraction does not explain the gap
falsification_criterion: If the far-field gap to its own ceiling equals the mid/near gap, the far-field deficit is geometry/annotation, not semantics -> H11 REJECTED and reclassified
decision: REJECTED as the dominant DA factor. See H11-alt and H18.

hypothesis: The far-field deficit is an annotation/evaluation artefact, not a semantic bottleneck
evidence_available: Ground truth has 0.0% of its drivable area in the top third of the 640 canvas; content occupies rows 140-500. The 'far-field collapse' disappears once the padding is removed.
intervention: STEP2: per-band mixed-block fraction, per-band GT area share, per-band boundary fraction; and the same banding applied to R0 which does not route detection through Z
prediction_if_true: If far-field mixed-block fraction is much higher, the lower IoU is partly an evaluation ceiling; if R0 does not show the same far-field collapse, the deficit is attributable to the R2 routing, not to the labels
falsification_criterion: If R0 and R2 collapse identically in the far field, the cause is the data, not the architecture
decision: SUPPORTED. The far-field deficit was an evaluation artefact. Any future banding must crop first.

hypothesis: DA is loss/supervision limited (far-field gradient is diluted)
evidence_available: Far field occupies a small fraction of image area, so even a large per-pixel error there may contribute little to the DA loss.
intervention: STEP2 loss-side statistics: per-band pixel share, per-band loss contribution share, foreground/background ratio, per-pixel loss contribution
prediction_if_true: Far-field pixels contribute far less to the DA loss than their error rate warrants
falsification_criterion: If per-band loss share is proportional to per-band error, H12 is REJECTED
decision: Statistics only; a loss intervention requires a separate gate

hypothesis: Task gradient conflict is the dominant limitation
evidence_available: All pairwise cosines on Z are ~0 (|cos| < 0.06 at every width). Probe C: forcing near-parity of gradient magnitude cost -13.07x noise mAP50 and returned +0.27x noise on DA.
intervention: Already intervened causally (lambda_det = 0.2 at 20ep, two widths)
prediction_if_true: REJECTED
falsification_criterion: Falsified by direct intervention with a manipulation check that passed (weighted det share fell from ~0.75 to 0.33/0.47)
decision: Closed. Do not repeat gradient balancing (explicitly forbidden as a repeat)

hypothesis: The shared representation itself is the dominant limitation
evidence_available: Probes A (per-task width), B (reconstruction receptive field and depth), C (gradient share) and Phase 3B/3C (wider Z) all failed to move DA or lane. But probe A at 20ep showed that changing ONLY the lane branch moved detection by -2.53x noise, so the tasks are coupled through Z.
intervention: Deferred: compare shared vs task-private Z at matched parameters (architecture stage, not Phase 5)
prediction_if_true: Sharing imposes a measurable cost on detection
falsification_criterion: If a private-Z variant at matched params is not better, sharing is not the binding constraint
decision: Cost of sharing is real for detection; sharing is NOT the main lever for segmentation. Architecture decision, post-Phase 5

hypothesis: Different tasks have fundamentally different bottleneck types
evidence_available: Detection scales with encoder capacity (Phase3A monotone, Phase3C encoder-heavy wins); lane sits exactly on a model-free resolution ceiling; DA is capacity-saturated but far-field deficient.
intervention: The whole of Phase 5 - this is the meta-hypothesis
prediction_if_true: No single intervention improves all three tasks; each task responds to a different axis
falsification_criterion: If any single intervention improves detection, DA and lane together by >= 2x noise, H15 is REJECTED

hypothesis: Lane's resolution bottleneck is threshold-like rather than gradual
evidence_available: Section 8 of the brief. The 1/8 ceiling is met exactly, which is what a hard geometric threshold looks like rather than a soft capacity limit.
intervention: Only decide after 1/4 and (conditionally) 1/2 are measured
prediction_if_true: 1/4 clears the ceiling substantially while 1/2 adds nothing
falsification_criterion: If gains are gradual across 1/8 -> 1/4 -> 1/2, the bottleneck is capacity-like, not a threshold
decision: Determines whether the result is a principle (threshold) or just another scaling curve

hypothesis: Lane has TWO stacked bottlenecks: quantisation (precision, the head cannot paint thinner than its grid) and continuity (recall, whole segments are missed). They have different fixes.
evidence_available: r0_z16: precision 0.2049, recall 0.6706, painted/GT area 3.55x, fg IoU 0.1845, against a 1/8 block-fill reference of 0.1854 (recall 1.0 by construction). The model is marginally MORE parsimonious than block-fill while missing a third of the target: it is trading recall for precision along the 1/8 isoquant. Label geometry rules out a width explanation for the misses - all 11-14 lane classes are 3.3-4.1 px - so a missed segment is missed for appearance or continuity reasons.
intervention: Decompose the probe result into precision and recall instead of reading fg IoU alone. A 1/4 head should move precision. If it moves recall too, continuity was downstream of resolution; if recall stays at 0.67, continuity is a separate bottleneck.
prediction_if_true: l14f1 raises precision above 0.2049 while recall stays near 0.67, leaving a residual recall gap that no resolution rung closes.
falsification_criterion: recall rises in proportion to precision, i.e. the missing segments were simply too thin to survive at 1/8 and reappear once the grid is finer.

hypothesis: DA is limited by region-level semantic identification (which regions count as drivable) rather than by resolution, boundary localisation or channel capacity.
evidence_available: r0_z16 DA: fg IoU 0.7699 vs a 1/8 block-fill reference of 0.8801 (delta -0.11); recall 0.9841 saturated; precision 0.7795; painted/GT area 1.319x; tolerance curve flat (tol0 0.7699 -> tol8 0.7951, only +0.025); boundary band holds 28.4% of foreground at the model's granularity. Flat tolerance rules out a thin misaligned rim; being below the block-fill reference rules out resolution; recall saturation rules out missed regions. What is left is over-inclusion.
intervention: Anatomy of the false positives (4B-4): connected-component size distribution, distance from each FP component to the nearest GT foreground, and whether components touch the image border. Blobs far from GT = semantic confusion; a <=2 px rim = boundary precision, which the flat tolerance curve already argues against.
prediction_if_true: FP components are large, contiguous, and located in places that look drivable but are not labelled - adjacent lanes beyond a median, turn pockets, road-like shoulders - rather than forming a rim around the true region.
falsification_criterion: FP is dominated by components within a few px of GT, or by a thin rim, which would put the error back on boundary localisation.
